title: burstbackoff-strategy-prototyping-notes
content:
Summary:

This doc captures a working idea and experiment notes for a probabilistic local backoff ("burstbackoff") mechanism to mitigate short-lived GPU pool degradation caused by noisy tenants and autoscaler misconfiguration. Goal is to reduce tail latency and eviction cascades while avoiding heavy-handed pool-level evictions that harm throughput.

Context / Motivation:
- Recurring incidents: intermittent 99th+ latency spikes across dedicated GPU pools correlated with sudden small bursts from single jobs (usually long-context chat or heavy beam search). On-call mitigation has often been: cordon instance, manual eviction, or scale-up which is slow/costly.
- Autoscaler config sometimes overshoots scale-down aggressively leading to noisy-neighbor amplification when capacity is tight.
- We need a minimizing-surface approach that: 
  - is safe to deploy as a per-node agent (low blast radius),
  - does not require immediate infra changes,
  - provides graceful degradation for noisy tenants and preserves fair throughput.

High-level idea (burstbackoff):
- Each serving VM/node maintains a short sliding window estimate of per-tenant (or per-job) request intensity and observed token-generation latencies.
- When a tenant exceeds a dynamic intensity threshold relative to node baseline, that tenant is sampled with probability p_backoff (function of intensity ratio). Sampled requests are either: 1) assigned lower scheduling priority, 2) slightly delayed (sleep 20-200ms) before scheduling, or 3) returned quickly with a transient 503 with Retry-After (configurable).
- The probability is calibrated so that single noisy jobs are damped quickly but large-scale coordinated traffic is not catastrophically shed.

Why probabilistic?
- Avoids synchronized shedding which can create oscillations and cascades across pool.
- Gives noisy jobs a chance to continue (soft-throttle) instead of immediate kill.
- Smooths client-side retry behavior (if we return 503+Retry-After, not all clients retry immediately).

Metrics to track (initial experiment):
- 99th / 99.9th generation latency per-pool and per-tenant (pre/post).
- Eviction rate (manual/automatic) per-day.
- Throughput tokens/sec per-pool.
- Tail error rate (503s introduced by burstbackoff).
- Autoscaler churn (scale-up/scale-down events) frequency.
- Client retries (if we instrument Retry-After handling).

Experiment plan (phase 0 -> 2):
- Phase 0 (simulation): replay traffic from last 30 days using synthetic noisy-job injection. Tune p_backoff function (sigmoid-ish) to target reducing 99.9p by ~40% on replay traces without increasing token cost > 5%.
- Phase 1 (canary): ship per-node agent to 2 small dedicated pools (dev/stage) with feature flag. Observe metrics for 48–72h. Default action: latency-insert (sleep 50ms) for sampled requests.
- Phase 2 (wider roll): enable on 25% of pools with priority-based scheduling fallback. Gradual rollout with circuit breaker (disable if eviction rate increases or throughput drops > 7%).

Quick operational runbook (for on-call):
1) When 99.9p latency spike observed on dedicated pools:
   - Check dashboards: "Dedicated Pool - 99.9 Latency", "Pool CPU/GPU utilization", "Per-tenant intensity heatmap".
   - If "burstbackoff" is enabled in that pool, look at agent logs (aggregated at /logs/burstbackoff) and check sampled rate and actions.
2) If abnormal high sampling (>=30%) correlates with a single tenant: 
   - Notify solutions-eng owner for that tenant (link via per-tenant metadata).
   - Temporarily toggle agent action to "logging-only" (no delays) via feature flag if false positives suspected.
3) If pool still degrading and sampling low: suspect autoscaler misconfig: check scaling events and scale-down cooldowns. Open INFR ticket if pattern repeats.
4) Escalation: cordon node and evict noisy VM if multi-node effects present.

Instrumentation / telemetry details:
- Agent exports Prometheus metrics: backoff_samples_total{pool,tenant,action}, backoff_sample_ratio, sample_latency_ms_histogram, sample_trigger_reason.
- Traces: attach sample decision as span attribute in request traces to correlate with tail latencies.
- Logs: structured JSON lines with tenant_id, job_id, intensity, sample_prob, action, decision_ts.

Configuration knobs (initial):
- baseline_window_secs (default 60)
- intensity_threshold_pct (default 300) // percent of baseline that triggers consideration
- min_sample_probability (default 0.05)
- max_sample_probability (default 0.6)
- delay_ms_range (20-200ms)
- action_mode: delay | priority_decrement | transient_503 | log_only
- cooloff_secs_per_tenant (how long reduced priority holds)

Safety and open questions:
- Fairness: how to avoid penalizing bursty-but-legitimate jobs (e.g., scheduled large-batch in enterprise SLA). Need allowlist mechanism by tenant tier and job tags.
- Security: ensure tenant_id attribution is correct and cannot be spoofed (source of truth: routing tokens).
- Client UX: if we return 503+Retry-After, client retry behavior must backoff appropriately. Many older clients may hammer; prefer delay/priority approach initially.
- Autoscaler interactions: could reduce observed intensity and cause over-scale-down. Need to coordinate with autoscaler: when burstbackoff active, autoscaler should treat sampled load as real load (or provide special signal).

Commands & quick checks (for debugging):
- List nodes with high sample rate: kubectl -n serving logs -l app=burstbackoff-agent --since=2h | jq 'select(.backoff_sample_ratio > 0.1) | {node, pool, tenant}'
- Query Prometheus: sum(rate(backoff_samples_total[5m])) by (pool, action)
- Check top tenants by intensity: /dashboards/pool-intensity?pool=<pool-id>

Notes from first simulation run (2025-02-25):
- When synthetic noisy job was a long-beam search with token rate 2.7x baseline, a sample_probability curve capped at 0.5 reduced 99.9p by 38% and increased 503s by 0.8% (acceptable).
- Delay-only mode introduced fewer retries than 503 mode in client replay.
- Autoscaler in test env scaled down aggressively after backoff reduced observed CPU usage; this caused a secondary spike. Need autoscaler feature flag to ignore short-lived backoff signals.

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Add allowlist based on tenant tier + job metadata (owner: Ravi).
- [ ] Implement feature-flagging via config-service and rollout UI (owner: Aisha).
- [ ] Add autoscaler compatibility signal (owner: Platform Eng). Create INFRA ticket.
- [ ] Run broader 7-day replay test with multiple simultaneous noisy jobs (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Draft short customer-facing note describing transient 503 behavior and expected retries (owner: Claire).

Open discussion points (notes to self):
- If we pursue this, consider renaming to "soft-shed" rather than burstbackoff — easier to sell.
- Could we push some of this logic to the router layer (global) to avoid per-node divergence? But router-level makes it easier to synchronise and harder to keep node-local fairness.
- How to measure non-functional impact (quality of generation) when delaying vs throwing 503s — need to add prompt-level eval hooks.

Slack/communication: #sre-dedicated-capacity for live ops. Use thread with PR link once prototype lands.

References & artifacts:
- Replay traces: s3://replay-archives/dedicated_pools/2024-11/
- Github proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789
- Related tickets: INFR-2456, INFRA-1123

Last thoughts:
This is an exploratory, low-risk mitigation that can be rolled back immediately. The key to success is strong telemetry and autoscaler coordination. Keep early deployment to non-prod and small pools only until we prove it doesn't cause scale-down cascades.

— Claire
